pointerGraceIntentRef.current?.side;\n      return isMovingTowards && isPointerInGraceArea(event, pointerGraceIntentRef.current?.area);\n    }, []);\n\n    return (\n      <MenuContentProvider\n        scope={__scopeMenu}\n        searchRef={searchRef}\n        onItemEnter={React.useCallback(\n          (event) => {\n            if (isPointerMovingToSubmenu(event)) event.preventDefault();\n          },\n          [isPointerMovingToSubmenu],\n        )}\n        onItemLeave={React.useCallback(\n          (event) => {\n            if (isPointerMovingToSubmenu(event)) return;\n            contentRef.current?.focus();\n            setCurrentItemId(null);\n          },\n          [isPointerMovingToSubmenu],\n        )}\n        onTriggerLeave={React.useCallback(\n          (event) => {\n            if (isPointerMovingToSubmenu(event)) event.preventDefault();\n          },\n          [isPointerMovingToSubmenu],\n        )}\n        pointerGraceTimerRef={pointerGraceTimerRef}\n        onPointerGraceIntentChange={React.useCallback((intent) => {\n          pointerGraceIntentRef.current = intent;\n        }, [])}\n      >\n        <ScrollLockWrapper {...scrollLockWrapperProps}>\n          <FocusScope\n            asChild\n            trapped={trapFocus}\n            onMountAutoFocus={composeEventHandlers(onOpenAutoFocus, (event) => {\n              // when opening, explicitly focus the content area only and leave\n              // `onEntryFocus` in  control of focusing first item\n              event.preventDefault();\n              contentRef.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true });\n            })}\n            onUnmountAutoFocus={onCloseAutoFocus}\n          >\n            <DismissableLayer\n              asChild\n onFocusOutside={onFocusOutside}\n              onInteractOutside={onInteractOutside}\n              onDismiss={onDismiss}\n            >\n              <RovingFocusGroup.Root\n focus first item when using keyboard\n                  if (!rootContext.isUsingKeyboardRef.current) event.preventDefault();\n                })}\n                preventScrollOnEntryFocus\n              >\n                <PopperPrimitive.Content\n                  role=\"menu\"\n                  aria-orientation=\"vertical\"\n                  data-state={getOpenState(context.open)}\n                  data-radix-menu-content=\"\"\n                  dir={rootContext.dir}\n                  {...popperScope}\n                  {...contentProps}\n                  ref={composedRefs}\n                  style={{ outline: 'none', ...contentProps.style }}\n                  onKeyDown={composeEventHandlers(contentProps.onKeyDown, (event) => {\n                    // submenu key events bubble through portals. We only care about keys in this menu.\n                    const target = event.target as HTMLElement;\n                    const isKeyDownInside =\n                      target.closest('[data-radix-menu-content]') === event.currentTarget;\n                    const isModifierKey = event.ctrlKey || event.altKey || event.metaKey;\n                    const isCharacterKey = event.key.length === 1;\n                    if (isKeyDownInside) {\n                      // menus should not be navigated using tab key so we prevent it\n                      if (event.key === 'Tab') event.preventDefault();\n                      if (!isModifierKey && isCharacterKey) handleTypeaheadSearch(event.key);\n                    }\n                    // focus first/last item based on key pressed\n                    const content = contentRef.current;\n                    if (event.target !== content) return;\n                    if (!FIRST_LAST_KEYS.includes(event.key)) return;\n                    event.preventDefault();\n                    const items = getItems().filter((item) => !item.disabled);\n                    const candidateNodes = items.map((item) => item.ref.current!);\n                    if (LAST_KEYS.includes(event.key)) candidateNodes.reverse();\n                    focusFirst(candidateNodes);\n                  })}\n                  onBlur={composeEventHandlers(props.onBlur, (event) => {\n                    // clear search buffer when leaving the menu\n                    if (!event.currentTarget.contains(event.target)) {\n                      window.clearTimeout(timerRef.current);\n                      searchRef.current = '';\n                    }\n                  })}\n                  onPointerMove={composeEventHandlers(\n                    props.onPointerMove,\n                    whenMouse((event) => {\n                      const target = event.target as HTMLElement;\n                      const pointerXHasChanged = lastPointerXRef.current !== event.clientX;\n\n                      // We don't use `event.movementX` for this check because Safari will\n                      // always return `0` on a pointer event.\n                      if (event.currentTarget.contains(target) && pointerXHasChanged) {\n                        const newDir = event.clientX > lastPointerXRef.current ? 'right' : 'left';\n                        pointerDirRef.current = newDir;\n                        lastPointerXRef.current = event.clientX;\n                      }\n                    }),\n                  )}\n                />\n              </RovingFocusGroup.Root>\n            </DismissableLayer>\n          </FocusScope>\n        </ScrollLockWrapper>\n      </MenuContentProvider>\n    );\n  },\n);\n\nMenuContent.displayName = CONTENT_NAME;\n\n/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n * MenuGroup\n * position recalculation is driven by resize/scroll/mutation observers, not by arbitrary JS mutations to a ref's closure state\n   - `DismissableLayer`'s `disableOutsidePointerEvents` behavior: sets `document.body.style.pointerEvents = 'none'` while a modal layer (default `modal=true` for ContextMenu) is open, and layers stack via `context.layersWithOutsidePointerEventsDisabled`\n   - React `useRef` identity stability — an object created once via `useRef({...})` never changes reference across renders, which affects reference-equality checks like `previousAnchor !== anchorRef.current`\n   - Native browser `contextmenu` event and `event.preventDefault()` — needed to suppress the native OS/browser context menu when the custom Radix menu should show instead\n   - Testing stack: Vitest + Testing Library (`fireEvent.contextMenu`, `screen`, `waitFor`) for unit tests in `context-menu.test.tsx`; 'auto' : 'none'` on itself when body pointer-events are globally disabled, to re-enable interaction just for the topmost/permitted layer(s). This means the layer's own subtree (the `MenuContent`) can still receive pointer events (via inline style `pointer-events: auto` override), but anything OUTSIDE any tracked layer/branch (like the raw trigger `<span>`, which is NOT a `DismissableLayerBranch` and not itself a layer) is still covered by `body { pointer-events: none }` and thus cannot receive pointer/contextmenu interaction — this is the crux of the suspected bug.\n     Also noted `DismissableLayerBranch` / `useDismissableLayerSurface` exports, used elsewhere only by `dialog.tsx` (via grep) — not currently used by `context-menu.tsx` or `menu.tsx` for the trigger element.\n\n   - `/app/packages/react/popper/src/popper.tsx` (489 lines) — fully read. Key relevant piece — `PopperAnchor`'s virtual-ref handling effect:\n     ```jsx\n     const anchorRef = React.useRef<Measurable | null>(null);\n     React.useEffect(() => {\n       if (!virtualRef) {\n         return;\n       }\n       const previousAnchor = anchorRef.current;\n       anchorRef.current = virtualRef.current;\n       if (previousAnchor !== anchorRef.current) {\n         onAnchorChange(anchorRef.current);\n       }\n     });\n     ```\n     This runs on every render (no dependency array) but compares `virtualRef.current` (a stable object identity, since `virtualRef` itself is a `useRef({...})` created once in `ContextMenuTrigger`) against the previously stored value. Because the object identity never changes across renders, `onAnchorChange` fires only ONCE ever (the first time `anchorRef.current` transitions from `null` to the virtualRef object) and never again — even though `pointRef.current` (read inside `getBoundingClientRect()`) is mutated on every right-click. This means `context.anchor` in Popper's context is set once and never \"changes\" from React's perspective, which likely prevents floating-ui's `useFloating`/`autoUpdate` from recognizing that a reposition is needed when the user right-clicks again at a new location while the menu is already open (since nothing signals a change: no resize, no scroll, no DOM mutation, no anchor object identity change).\n     Also read `PopperContent`'s `useFloftware `useFloating` call: `elements: { reference: context.anchor }`, with `whileElementsMounted: autoUpdate(...)`.\n\n   - `/app/apps/ssr-testing/app/context-menu/page.tsx` — simple demo page using `ContextMenu.Root`/`Trigger`/`Portal`/`Content` with Undo/Redo/Cut/Copy/Paste items; reviewed for context but not modified.\n\n   - `/app/packages/react/dropdown-menu/src/dropdown-menu.tsx` — partially read (lines 1–140) for comparison; noted `DropdownMenuTrigger`'s `onPointerDown` pattern using `composeEventHandlers` and explicit `event.button === 0` / `ctrlKey` checks — not directly used for the fix but examined as a sibling primitive pattern.\n\n   - CHANGELOG.md files for `context-menu`, `dismissable-layer`, and `menu` packages — skimmed; no existing changelog entry matches this exact bug (nothing about \"right click again while open\" or reposition-on-reopen). Problem Solving:\n   - Established strong circumstantial evidence for two compounding root causes:\n     (a) `ContextMenuTrigger`'s `onContextMenu` handler (mouse path) unconditionally calls `context.onOpenChange(true)` without first closing if already open — unlike the touch/pen `onPointerDown` path, which explicitly does `if (context.open) { context.onOpenChange(false); }` before reopening. Because `useControllableState` no-ops when setting the same value, calling `onOpenChange(true)` while already open does not change the open state and won't force any position/content re-evaluation.\n     (b) Even if a reposition were attempted, `PopperAnchor`'s virtual-ref-change-detection effect in `popper.tsx` compares object identity (`previousAnchor !== anchorRef.current`), but the `virtualRef` ref object created in `ContextMenuTrigger` is stable across renders (created once via `useRef`), so `onAnchorChange` never fires again after the initial mount — meaning floating-ui's positioning system is never told to recompute even if `pointRef.current` (the click coordinates) changes.\n     (c) Additionally, since `ContextMenu` defaults to `modal = true`, `DismissableLayer` sets `document.body.style.pointerEvents = 'none'` while open (confirmed by the existing \"disables pointer events on the body while a modal menu is open\" test) — this could prevent the raw trigger `<span>` (which is not wrapped in a `DismissableLayerBranch`/dismissable-layer-surface) from ever receiving the second `contextmenu` event at all, which would explain why the native browser context menu appears instead of the custom Radix menu reacting (since `event.preventDefault()` in the trigger's `onContextMenu` handler never executes if the event never reaches it).\n   - These three factors together are consistent with the GIF's visual narrative (custom menu opens once and stays fixed in place; subsequent right-clicks at different locations show the native browser menu instead of moving/reopening the custom menu).\n   - No fix has been implemented yet. No test has been added yet. No lint/format/test/typecheck commands have been run yet.\n\n6.
